title: How much does fridge repair cost in Soweto?
meta_title: Fridge repair cost in Soweto - simple guide
meta_description: Find out what you can expect to pay for fridge repair in Soweto, including the R250.00 call-out fee and why costs vary. Get clear advice now.
excerpt: Learn the real cost of fridge repair in Soweto, the R250.00 call-out fee and what factors affect the final price.
body:
When your fridge stops keeping food cold, the first question is always about cost. In Soweto the call-out fee is R250.00 and it’s waived if we carry out the repair. The total price then depends on the exact fault, which we identify before giving you a quote. Below we explain the common problems, what you can check yourself, and why the repair price varies.

## Common reasons a fridge stops cooling

- **Blocked airflow** - Food or ice packed against the rear vent stops cold air from reaching the fridge compartment.
- **Defrost fault** - A failed defrost heater, sensor or timer lets ice build up on the cooling coil, so the freezer stays cold but the fridge warms.
- **Fan not running** - A dead evaporator fan traps cold air, while a dead condenser fan can overheat the compressor and make it shut down.
- **Compressor or start relay issue** - A humming compressor that clicks and stops often means the start relay has failed; this is cheaper than a full compressor replacement.
- **Gas leak** - If the compressor runs constantly with no cooling, the refrigerant may have escaped and needs a professional leak-find and refill.

These are the faults we test for in the order listed, so you only pay for the part that really needs fixing.

## What you can safely check before calling a technician

- **Settings** - Make sure the temperature dial or digital display hasn’t been bumped and that any demo or holiday mode is off.
- **Vent clearance** - Move any food that’s touching the rear vent and brush dust off the coil if you can see it.
- **Door seal** - Close a sheet of paper in the door; if it slides out easily the seal isn’t holding.
- **Water leak clues** - Look for a small hole in the drain channel at the back wall and clear it gently with warm water. Also check that the fridge leans slightly backwards so water can flow to the tray.
- **Noise or smell** - If you hear loud clicking every few minutes, smell burning, or the fridge trips the electricity, switch it off at the wall and leave it off until a technician arrives.

Never open panels, touch wires or try to reset a relay yourself - let a technician handle those parts.

## Why repair costs differ

The price you pay after the R250.00 call-out depends on the part that needs replacement and the labour involved.

- **Fan replacement** - Usually a simple, low-cost job because the fan itself is inexpensive.
- **Defrost heater or sensor** - Slightly more labour, but still a modest part price.
- **Start relay** - One of the cheapest fixes; the relay is a small component.
- **Compressor** - This is the most expensive part and labour, as it may involve removing the sealed system.
- **Gas leak repair** - Requires a leak-find test and a refrigerant refill, which adds both parts and specialist labour.

We always test first, identify the exact fault and then give you a clear quote before any work starts. That way you never pay for an unnecessary replacement.

## What to expect from our mobile service

- **Same-day response** - We come to your home in Soweto and 19 other areas around Johannesburg.
- **R250.00 call-out** - This fee is deducted if we carry out the repair.
- **9-month guarantee** - All repairs are covered for nine months, giving you peace of mind.
- **Transparent pricing** - After testing we tell you exactly what part is needed and why, then provide the final cost.
- **Safety first** - If we detect a burning smell, loud clicking or an electrical trip, we will switch the appliance off at the wall and advise you to keep the area clear until the repair is done.

## What to do while you wait for the repair

- Keep the fridge and freezer doors closed; a full freezer holds its cold much longer than an open one.
- Move perishable items like meat and milk to a neighbour’s fridge or a cooler box with ice if the temperature has risen above 5 °C for more than a few hours.
- Do **not** chip ice with a knife - you could puncture the gas line and cause a bigger problem.
- If there is water on the floor, switch the fridge off at the wall and dry the area before touching anything.

These steps help preserve your food and keep the area safe until we arrive.

## How to book a repair

Simply WhatsApp or call us on **060 432 2996**. Tell us the suburb (Orlando East, Diepkloof, Meadowlands, etc.) and a brief description of the problem. Send a photo of the model sticker too. We test the fridge first and give you the price before we start.

faqs.q: What does the R250.00 call-out fee cover?
faqs.a: The R250.00 fee covers the technician’s travel to your home and the initial diagnostic test. If we repair the fridge, the fee is deducted from the final bill.

faqs.q: Can I fix a noisy fan myself?
faqs.a: No. While you can check that nothing is blocking the fan, opening the fridge to replace the fan should be done by a technician to avoid injury or further damage.

faqs.q: My fridge is leaking water - should I turn it off?
faqs.a: If water is pooling near the plug or compressor, switch the fridge off at the wall and dry the floor. Then call us so we can clear the drain or repair the line safely.

faqs.q: Why does my fridge keep freezing food?
faqs.a: Common causes are a faulty temperature sensor, a stuck damper flap, or a thermostat that’s stuck closed. We’ll test the sensor and damper and replace only the part that’s faulty.

title: Repair or Replace a Broken Appliance in South Africa - What to Choose
meta_title: Repair or Replace Appliance South Africa - Decision Guide
meta_description: Learn when to repair or replace a faulty fridge, stove or washing machine in South Africa. Get clear checks and know the costs before you decide.
excerpt: Decide if you should repair or replace a broken appliance with simple checks, cost hints and expert advice for South African homes.
body:
When an appliance stops working you face a choice: spend money fixing it or buy a new one. The decision isn’t always obvious, especially with the cost of call-outs and parts. This guide walks you through the key checks for fridges, stoves and washing machines, explains the most common faults and helps you weigh repair costs against replacement. By the end you’ll know when a quick fix is worth it and when it’s time to start shopping for a new unit.

## Identify the Symptom First

Start by describing exactly what’s wrong. A fridge that’s warm, a stove plate that stays cold, or a washing machine that won’t spin each point to a different set of likely faults. Write down:
- What you hear (fans, clicks, humming)
- Any smells (burnt plastic, electrical ozone)
- Which settings you tried (high, low, different knobs)
- Whether other parts on the same appliance still work
These details give a technician a clear picture and prevent unnecessary parts being ordered.

## When a Stove Plate Won’t Heat

A single cold plate on an otherwise functional stove is usually a cheap repair. Look for these signs:
- **Cracked or bulged plate** - the metal may be deformed when it’s cold.
- **Switch wear** - the plate heats on some knob positions but not others.
- **Burnt connector** - a faint burnt smell indicates the wire under the plate may have overheated.
- **Indicator light out** - the plate can still heat even if the light is dead.
**Owner checks:** Try every knob setting. If heat appears on some positions, the switch or a part of the plate is likely at fault. Do not open the hob; the wiring is live even with the knobs off. If you notice any burnt smell, switch the stove off at the wall and call a technician.
**Cost hint:** Most plate replacements cost well under the price of a new stove, especially when the rest of the unit is in good condition.

## Fridge Not Cooling - Common Causes

If the interior light works but food stays warm, the fridge has power but something that creates or moves cold is failing. Check these areas:
- **Blocked airflow** - move food away from the rear vent and ensure nothing is packed against it.
- **Defrost fault** - ice buildup behind the panel stops cold from reaching the fridge.
- **Evaporator fan dead** - without the fan, cold stays trapped in the freezer.
- **Condenser fan dead** - the compressor can overheat and shut down.
- **Start relay** - a humming compressor that clicks and stops often points to a relay issue, which is cheaper than a new compressor.
- **Gas leak** - if the compressor runs all day with no cooling, the refrigerant may have escaped.
**Owner checks:** Verify the temperature dial isn’t set to a demo mode. Feel the back or sides; they should be warm, not hot. Brush dust off the condenser coil and give the fridge space to breathe. Close a piece of paper in the door; if it slides out easily, the seal is faulty. If you smell burning or hear loud clicking every few minutes, switch the fridge off at the wall and call a technician.
**Cost hint:** Replacing a fan or relay is usually far cheaper than a new fridge. A full compressor replacement can approach the price of a new unit, especially for larger models.

## Fridge Freezing Food When It Shouldn't

When lettuce turns icy and milk becomes slushy, the fridge is running nonstop. Typical reasons include:
- **Faulty temperature sensor** - it reads too warm, so the fridge never shuts off.
- **Damper stuck open** - the flap that controls airflow between freezer and fridge stays open, sending too much cold air.
- **Worn thermostat** - contacts can stick closed on simple dial models.
- **Food blocking the vent** - items placed directly in front of the vent freeze first.
**Owner checks:** Set the thermostat to the middle position and wait a full day before judging. Keep wet vegetables away from the back vent. Place a glass of water on the middle shelf; it should be 3-5 °C in the morning. If a sheet of ice builds on the back wall, switch the fridge off at the wall and let it defrost with the door open, do not scrape the ice.
**Cost hint:** Sensor or damper replacements are usually inexpensive. If the thermostat is the problem, a new dial unit can be a low-cost fix.

## Washing Machine Won’t Spin or Drain

The same simple checks apply to washing machines:
- **Hoses and filters** - look for kinks, blockages or lint buildup.
- **Door lock** - if the door isn’t sealing, the machine won’t spin.
- **Power supply** - ensure the plug is firmly in the socket and the breaker isn’t tripped.
- **Leveling** - an un-level machine can cause vibration and stop the spin cycle.
**Owner checks:** Move the machine a few centimetres to level it, clean the filter, and listen for the spin motor humming. If you hear a loud click and the drum stays still, switch the machine off at the wall and call a technician.
**Cost hint:** Replacing a pump or belt is generally cheaper than buying a new washer, especially for mid-range models.

## When to Replace Instead of Repair

Consider replacement when:
- The appliance is more than 8-10 years old and parts are hard to find.
- Multiple components have failed, making repair costs approach the price of a new unit.
- Energy efficiency is poor; a newer model can save on electricity, especially during load-shedding periods.
- A geyser tank is leaking, or a fridge needs a compressor that costs close to a new one.
If you’re unsure, request a test from a technician. The call-out is R250.00, and if we carry out the repair the fee is waived. After testing we’ll give you a clear price and a recommendation.
**Switch off and call:** For any fault that produces a burning smell, loud repeated clicking, or if the appliance trips the electricity, turn it off at the wall and contact us immediately.

## Getting Help in Soweto and Surrounds

Our mobile service brings the technician to your home. We cover Soweto, Roodepoort, Johannesburg, Randburg, Sandton, Midrand, Fourways, Kempton Park, Germiston, Boksburg, Lenasia, Randfontein, Krugersdorp, Alberton, Benoni, Edenvale, Bedfordview, Brakpan, Eldorado Park and Ennerdale. Call or WhatsApp 060 432 2996 for a same-day visit. The call-out is R250.00, free if we repair, and every repair comes with a 9-month guarantee.

faqs.q: How much does a fridge repair usually cost in Soweto?
faqs.a: The call-out is R250.00 (free if we fix it). The rest depends on the part: a fan, relay or sensor costs far less than a compressor. We give you a clear price after testing.

faqs.q: What should I check before calling a technician for a cold stove plate?
faqs.a: Try every knob setting; note if the plate heats on some positions. Look for cracks or a domed surface when the plate is cold. If you smell burnt plastic, switch the stove off at the wall and call us.

faqs.q: My fridge is warm but the light works - what’s the first thing to do?
faqs.a: Move any food away from the rear vent, brush dust off the condenser coil and feel the back for excessive heat. If the back is very hot or you hear loud clicking, turn the fridge off at the wall and wait for a technician.

faqs.q: When is it better to buy a new washing machine rather than repair it?
faqs.a: If the machine is over 8-10 years old, has multiple failed parts, or the repair estimate is close to the price of a new model, replacement is usually smarter. Energy-efficient newer models can also lower your electricity bill.

title: Why Power Cuts and Surges Damage Fridges and How to Protect Yours
meta_description: Learn how power cuts and surges can break your fridge and what simple steps protect it. Get practical advice and know when to call a Soweto technician.
excerpt: Power cuts and surges can ruin a fridge; follow these checks and protection tips to keep it running.
body:
Power cuts and sudden surges are a regular part of life in many South African homes. When they hit your fridge, the result can be a noisy compressor, a warm freezer or even a total breakdown. Here is why it happens, the easiest ways to protect your fridge, what you can safely check and when to call a technician.

## How Sudden Power Changes Harm the Cooling System

When the supply drops, the fridge’s compressor may stall. When power returns, a surge can force a large inrush current through the start relay and compressor motor. This can:
- Overheat the **compressor** and cause it to click then shut down.
- Burn out the **start relay** so the motor never turns on.
- Damage the **control board** that tells the fan and defrost heater when to work.
The result is a fridge that runs hot, makes loud clicking noises, or stops cooling altogether.

If you notice a humming compressor that clicks and then goes quiet after a load-shedding event, the start relay is a likely culprit. If the fridge trips the electricity or you smell burning, switch it off at the wall and call a technician right away.

## Owner Checks After a Power Cut or Surge

Before you call a repair person, do these safe checks:
- **Look** at the front dial or digital display. Make sure it hasn’t been bumped into a demo or holiday mode.
- **Listen** for the evaporator fan (inside the freezer) and the condenser fan (at the back). If either is silent, the fan may have failed.
- **Feel** the sides and back of the fridge. Warm is normal, but a very hot surface means the compressor can’t get rid of heat.
- **Check** the door seal by sliding a sheet of paper into the door. If it slides out easily, the seal isn’t holding and the fridge works harder.
- **Inspect** the back vent and coil. Brush away dust and give the unit space to breathe.
- **Smell** for any burning odor. If you detect it, turn the fridge off at the wall and wait for a technician.
These steps help you spot a blocked airflow, a dead fan or a faulty relay without opening the appliance.

## Common Faults Triggered by Power Issues

Power problems often expose the same weak points that cause regular fridge failures:
- **Blocked airflow** - Food packed against the rear vent or ice buildup behind the panel stops cold from reaching the fridge compartment.
- **Defrost fault** - A failed defrost heater, sensor or timer lets ice build up on the cooling coil, turning the freezer into a solid block of ice while the fridge warms.
- **Fan failure** - If the evaporator fan stops, cold stays trapped in the freezer. If the condenser fan stops, the compressor overheats and cuts out.
- **Compressor or start relay** - A humming compressor that clicks and stops is often a relay that can’t handle the surge current.
- **Gas leak** - After a severe surge the compressor may run continuously without producing cold, indicating a possible refrigerant leak.
Understanding these patterns lets you explain to the technician what you observed, speeding up the diagnosis.

## Simple Ways to Protect Your Fridge from Surges

1. **Use a surge protector strip** designed for high-current appliances. Plug the fridge’s power cord into the strip and then into the wall socket. The strip will absorb spikes before they reach the compressor.
2. **Install a voltage stabiliser** if you live in an area with frequent fluctuations. A stabiliser keeps the voltage within safe limits for the fridge’s motor and electronics.
3. **Keep the fridge level and well-ventilated**. A level unit reduces strain on the compressor, and clean coils improve heat dissipation, making the fridge less vulnerable to overheating after a surge.
4. **Avoid over-loading the fridge**. Too many items block the internal fan and force the compressor to work harder, increasing the chance of a failure when power returns.
5. **Turn the fridge off at the wall** during prolonged load-shedding periods. This prevents repeated start-up surges when the power comes back.
6. **Regularly clean the condenser coil** at the back. Dust acts like an insulator and makes the compressor run hotter, which magnifies the effect of any surge.
These are small habits that help a fridge last longer.

## When to Call a Soweto Technician

If after the checks you notice any of the following, it’s time to call a professional:
- The fridge makes loud clicking every few minutes or the compressor hums then stops.
- The fridge trips the electricity or you smell burning.
- The freezer is covered in a sheet of ice and the fridge stays warm.
- The fan(s) are silent even though the fridge is plugged in.
- The temperature sensor seems off - a glass of water left on the middle shelf stays below 3 °C all night.
Our mobile service will come to your home, test fans, sensors, defrost heater, relay and compressor in that order, and only check for a gas leak if the frost pattern points to it. The call-out is R250.00, free if we carry out the repair, and we guarantee the work for nine months.

## What to Do While You Wait for a Repair

- **Keep the doors closed**. A full freezer holds its cold much longer than an open one.
- **Move perishable food** to a neighbour’s fridge or a cooler box with ice if the temperature has risen above 5 °C for more than a few hours.
- **Do not chip ice** with a knife; you could puncture the gas line and cause a costly leak.
- **Leave the fridge door open** only if you need to defrost a thick ice sheet. Let it melt naturally; do not scrape it.
These actions protect your food and prevent further damage while you wait for the technician.

faqs.q: Why does my fridge click and then stop after a power surge?
faqs.a: A surge can overload the start relay, causing the compressor to hum, click and shut down. The relay needs replacement, which a technician can diagnose and fix.

faqs.q: Can I use a regular power strip for my fridge?
faqs.a: Only a surge protector rated for high-current appliances should be used. Regular strips won’t absorb the large spikes that can damage the compressor.

faqs.q: My freezer is full of ice but the fridge is warm - what’s wrong?
faqs.a: That’s a classic defrost fault. Ice has built up on the cooling coil, stopping cold from reaching the fridge compartment. A technician will test the defrost heater, sensor and timer.

faqs.q: Is it safe to keep the fridge on during load-shedding?
faqs.a: Repeated start-up after a cut can stress the compressor. Turning the fridge off at the wall during long outages reduces the risk of surge-related damage.

title: Samsung washing machine error codes explained in plain English
meta_title: Samsung washing machine error codes explained
meta_description: Learn what Samsung washing machine error codes mean and how to check your machine before calling a technician.
excerpt: Understand Samsung washing machine error codes and simple owner checks before calling a technician.
body:
If your Samsung washing machine shows an error code, you don’t need to panic. Most codes point to something you can check in a few minutes: the tap, the filter, the hose, the door or the load. Below is what each one means, what to try and when to stop and call.

## What the code is really telling you

Samsung codes point to a system that is not working, not a specific part. **5E and 5C** mean the machine can’t get rid of water. **OE** means there is too much water in the drum. **4E or 4C** mean water isn’t getting in fast enough. **UE / Ub** warn of an unbalanced load. **dE / dC** are door-lock alerts. **HE** signals a heating issue, **LE** a leak or low level, **3E** a motor warning, and **tE** a temperature-sensor fault. Knowing this helps you decide whether a quick owner check will solve the problem or if you need a technician.

## Drain and overfill problems - codes 5E, 5C and OE

- Switch the machine off at the wall.
- Place a shallow tray and towels in front of the filter flap.
- Unscrew the filter slowly; let the water drain bit by bit.
- Remove any coins, hair clips, baby socks or school badges you see.
- Straighten the drain hose - pushing the machine back can flatten it.
- Run a drain or spin programme.
- If the pump hums but no water moves, or the filter is clean and the hose is straight, the pump may have failed and needs a technician.
- For OE, switch off and close the tap. The inlet valve may be stuck open or the level sensor may have failed, and a technician needs to test it.

## Spin problems - codes UE, Ub and 3E

- Open the door and spread the laundry evenly; a single heavy blanket can unbalance the drum.
- Add a few towels to a light load or remove items to achieve balance.
- Press down on the empty drum; it should rise and settle once, not bounce wildly.
- Run a drain programme and listen for the pump - a humming motor with no spin may indicate a worn belt, brushes or motor.
- If the drum still won’t spin after re-balancing, the suspension rods may be worn; stop trying and call a technician.
- For 3E, switch off for a few minutes, then try a small, balanced load. If the error returns, the motor or its sensor needs testing.

## Door-lock alerts - codes dE and dC

- Look for clothing caught in the door seal and remove it.
- Close the door firmly; you should hear a click.
- If the code stays after a firm close, the door lock mechanism is faulty and requires a professional repair.

## Water-supply and heating - codes 4E, 4C and HE

- Open the water tap fully; make sure the inlet hose is straight.
- At the hose-machine junction, remove the small mesh filter and rinse any debris.
- If water is still not filling, the inlet valve may need testing - call us.
- For HE, select a cold programme. If the machine washes fine on cold, the heater or its wiring is at fault and should be inspected by a technician.

## Leak or low-level warnings - code LE

- Switch off the machine and close the tap.
- Look under the appliance for any puddles.
- Check that the drain hose isn’t hanging too low; it should be at the recommended height.
- If you see water pooling inside the drum or on the floor, stop using the machine and call a technician.

faqs.q: What should I do if my Samsung washer shows a 5E error?
faqs.a: Turn the machine off at the wall, clean the pump filter and straighten the drain hose. Run a drain programme. If water still won’t leave or the pump hums without moving water, call a technician.

faqs.q: Why does my washer keep showing UE or Ub during spin cycles?
faqs.a: The load is likely unbalanced. Spread the laundry evenly or add a few towels to balance a heavy item. If the error appears on every load, the suspension may be worn and needs professional attention.

faqs.q: My machine won’t fill with water and shows 4E. Is it my fault?
faqs.a: Check that the tap is fully open and the inlet hose isn’t kinked. Clean the small mesh filter where the hose meets the machine. If water still won’t flow, the inlet valve may be faulty and should be inspected.

faqs.q: When is it safe to open the filter during a drain error?
faqs.a: Only after you have switched the machine off at the wall and placed towels to catch water. Open the filter slowly so the water drains gradually, then clean any debris.

title: Fridge Warm but Freezer Cold - What It Means and What to Do
meta_title: Fridge Warm but Freezer Cold - Quick Guide
meta_description: Find out why your fridge is warm while the freezer stays cold, the checks you can do yourself, and when to call a technician.
excerpt: Your fridge is warm but the freezer is still cold - learn the likely causes, safe owner checks and when to call a repair technician.
body:
If the freezer is still chilly but the fridge compartment feels warm, the appliance has power but something that moves or creates cold isn’t working right. In most South African homes the problem is either blocked airflow, a fan that’s stopped, a defrost fault or a compressor issue. Below you’ll find simple checks you can do yourself and clear signs that it’s time to call a professional.

## Check the Settings and Door Seal

- Make sure the temperature dial or digital display hasn’t been bumped into a demo or holiday mode.
- Close a sheet of paper in the fridge door; if it slides out easily the seal isn’t holding and warm air can creep in.
- Look around the door gasket for tears or gaps. A leaking seal often makes the fridge warm before the freezer does.
- If you notice the fridge is unusually hot to the touch on the sides or back, that could mean the condenser can’t get rid of heat - give it space and brush off any dust from the coils.

## Look for Blocked Airflow

- In most no-frost models the cold is produced in the freezer and blown into the fridge through vents at the back. Remove any food that is packed directly against these vents.
- Open the freezer and check for ice buildup on the rear wall or around the fan cover. Ice can act like a wall, stopping the cold air from reaching the fridge.
- If you see a thin layer of frost on the back wall, switch the fridge off and let it melt with the door open. Do not chip it with a knife.
- After clearing the area, give the fridge a few minutes to see if the fridge temperature starts to drop.

## Listen and Smell for Fan or Compressor Problems

- Stand close to the fridge and listen for the evaporator fan (inside the freezer) and the condenser fan (behind the unit). Both should run quietly when the compressor is on.
- If you hear no fan noise at all, the fan may have stopped - this traps cold air in the freezer and leaves the fridge warm.
- A loud clicking sound every few minutes, or a humming that stops after a few seconds, often points to a failed start relay or a compressor that is shutting down to protect itself.
- Any burning smell or frequent tripping of the electricity is a safety signal. Switch the fridge off at the wall and call a technician immediately.

## Check for Defrost Issues

- No-frost fridges have a defrost heater that melts any ice on the evaporator coil. If the heater, sensor or timer fails, ice can build up and block airflow.
- Look for a thick layer of ice on the freezer’s rear wall that doesn’t melt when you open the door. That’s a classic sign of a defrost fault.
- While the freezer may stay cold for a short while, the fridge will become warm first because the cold can’t be pushed through the vent.
- Do not try to remove the ice with a knife; instead, turn the fridge off, let it defrost naturally, and call a technician to test the defrost circuit.

## When to Call a Technician

- If you have checked the settings, seal, airflow and fans and the fridge is still warm, the problem is likely inside the compressor, start relay or a gas leak.
- A compressor that hums then clicks off, or a start relay that never engages, needs a professional test. Replacing a relay is cheaper than a whole compressor.
- Gas leaks are rare but possible; only a technician should locate and repair them.
- Our mobile service will come to your home, test the fans, sensors, defrost heater, relay and compressor in that order, and only then look for a leak if the frost pattern suggests it. Call or WhatsApp us at 060 432 2996 - the call-out is R250.00, free if we carry out the repair.

## What to Do While You Wait for a Repair

- Keep both doors closed as much as possible; a full freezer holds its cold longer than an open one.
- If the fridge has been above 5 °C for more than a few hours, move perishable items like meat and milk to a neighbour’s fridge or a cooler with ice packs.
- Do not attempt to chip ice with a knife - you could puncture the refrigerant line and cause a costly leak.
- Ensure the fridge is level, slightly tipped backwards, so the drain can flow to the tray at the bottom.
- If water is pooling under the drawers, check the drain hole at the back wall and clear any blockage with warm water.

faqs.q: Why is my fridge warm while the freezer is still cold?
faqs.a: The freezer makes the cold and pushes it into the fridge. If airflow is blocked, a fan has stopped, the defrost heater is stuck on ice, or the compressor can’t run properly, the fridge will warm before the freezer does.

faqs.q: What simple checks can I do before calling a technician?
faqs.a: Check the temperature dial isn’t on demo mode, test the door seal with a piece of paper, move food away from the vents, listen for the fans, and look for ice on the freezer’s rear wall. If any of these reveal a problem, you may need a professional.

faqs.q: When should I switch the fridge off at the wall and call for help?
faqs.a: If you smell burning, hear loud clicking every few minutes, see the compressor humming then stopping, or the appliance trips the electricity, turn it off at the wall right away and call a technician.

faqs.q: How long will a technician take to diagnose the problem?
faqs.a: We test the fans, defrost circuit, relay and compressor in that order, then check for a leak only if needed. The diagnosis is done on the spot, and you’ll get a price after testing.

title: Washing machine stuck with water inside? What to do first
meta_title: Washing machine full of water - quick owner checks
meta_description: Your washing machine won’t drain and the drum is full of water. Follow these simple steps before calling a technician - click for the full guide.
excerpt: Your washing machine won’t drain and the drum is full of water - try these easy checks before calling a tech.
body:
If your washing machine has stopped mid-cycle with a drum full of grey water, the first thing to do is turn it off at the wall and check the most common culprits. A blocked pump filter, a kinked drain hose or a simple house-drain blockage often cause the problem, and you can clear them yourself before a technician is needed.

## Turn the machine off safely

**Switch off the washing machine at the wall**. Wait a minute for any moving parts to stop. If the water in the drum is hot, let it cool before you open the filter. This protects you from burns and stops the machine from restarting while you work.

## Check the pump filter

The pump filter is the most frequent cause of a drainage failure.
- Place a shallow tray and a few towels on the floor in front of the filter flap.
- Unscrew the filter slowly; water will pour out gradually. Let it drain into the tray.
- Look inside for coins, hair clips, baby socks, school badges or any other debris.
- Remove anything you find and rinse the filter under running water.
- Re-screw the filter securely before you run a drain or spin programme.
If the water is still not draining after a clean, the pump itself may be faulty and will need a professional test.

## Inspect the drain hose

A hose that is folded, kinked or pushed too far into the wall can stop water from leaving the machine.
- Pull the washing machine gently forward just enough to see the hose.
- Straighten any bends and make sure the hose is not crushed.
- Check the hose end in the wall drain - it should sit loosely, not deep inside the pipe.
- If the hose looks damaged, straighten it or replace it when a technician arrives.

## Look at the house drain

Sometimes the problem isn’t the machine at all.
- Run a bucket of water down the same wall drain the washing machine uses.
- If the water backs up or drains very slowly, the house drain is blocked.
- In that case you’ll need a plumber to clear the pipe; the washing machine is fine.

## Run a test cycle

After you have cleaned the filter and checked the hose:
1. Switch the machine back on at the wall.
2. Select a **drain or spin programme**.
3. Listen for the pump - it should make a low humming sound and you should hear water moving.
If the drum empties, the problem was the filter or hose. If the drum stays full and the pump is silent, the pump may have failed and will need a technician to test and replace it.

## When to call a technician

Call Soweto Appliance Repairs if:
- The pump makes no sound at all after you’ve cleared the filter.
- Water still won’t drain even after the hose and house drain are verified clear.
- You notice any unusual smells (burnt electronics) or the machine stops halfway repeatedly.
- The display shows a drain code such as **5E** or **5C** and the above checks haven’t solved it.

faqs.q: Why does my washing machine show error code 5E?
faqs.a: Code 5E means the machine has detected a problem with the drain system. It could be a blocked pump filter, a kinked hose or a failed pump. Start by cleaning the filter and checking the hose before calling a technician.

faqs.q: What should I do if the water in the drum is hot?
faqs.a: Let the water cool before you open the filter. Hot water can cause burns and may also damage seals if you force the filter open too quickly.

faqs.q: Can a low water pressure affect the drain?
faqs.a: Low pressure mainly affects filling, not draining. However, if the house drain is partially blocked, water may back up and appear as a drainage issue. Test the wall drain with a bucket of water to be sure.

faqs.q: How long does a typical drain repair take?
faqs.a: It depends on the cause. Clearing a filter or hose is quick, while a failed pump has to be replaced. The technician will tell you after testing.
